# ScriptScan — Compliance Memorandum

**To:** Pharmacist-Owner, [Independent Ontario Pharmacy]
**From:** AI Legal-Research Team (General Counsel function)
**Re:** Lawfulness of deploying ScriptScan (local-mask-then-cloud prescription pre-fill tool) under Ontario health-privacy law
**Date:** June 18, 2026

---

## 1. Disclaimer

This memorandum is an **informational compliance analysis generated by an AI legal-research team**. It is **not legal advice**, does not create a solicitor-client relationship, and must not be relied upon as a legal opinion. The analysis synthesizes statute text, regulator guidance, and vendor documentation, and several conclusions were deliberately downgraded by an adversarial review because they turn on fact-specific determinations that only a licensed professional can make. **Before deploying ScriptScan in production, engage a licensed Ontario health-privacy lawyer** (and, ideally, a qualified re-identification-risk assessor). Where this memo says "compliant," read it as "appears aligned with the cited requirement on the facts described" — not as certification.

---

## 2. Bottom Line Up Front

**Can ScriptScan be used lawfully in an Ontario independent pharmacy? Conditionally yes — but not as currently described, and not without a lawyer's sign-off on the two load-bearing questions.**

**Overall residual risk rating: MODERATE-to-HIGH as currently designed → reducible to LOW-MODERATE with the safeguards in §5.**

The architecture's privacy-by-design intent (on-device masking, in-memory processing, no default persistence, mandatory pharmacist verification) is genuinely strong and materially reduces exposure. The pharmacist's verification workflow is the design's strongest point and is well-aligned with regulator expectations. However, two questions are decisive and **both are unresolved on the facts given**:

1. **Is the masked clinical image truly "de-identified" under PHIPA?** Almost certainly *not reliably*, because (a) the masking is heuristic OCR that the design itself admits can miss tokens, and (b) even a perfect mask leaves powerful quasi-identifiers — named prescriber + drug + strength + SIG + date — that can re-identify a patient in a small catchment. If de-identification fails, **real PHI is being disclosed cross-border to a US provider.**

2. **Is there a PHIPA-compliant agreement and configuration with Anthropic?** Not on the facts described. Standard commercial API terms are *not* a PHIPA agent/ESP agreement; Zero-Data-Retention (ZDR) and a HIPAA BAA are opt-in and not default; and the local Claude Code CLI path is **not HIPAA-eligible**.

The design is defensible **if** you (i) treat the masked image as PHI rather than assuming it is de-identified, (ii) put the correct contracts and configuration in place with Anthropic, (iii) make the PHI mask a fail-closed pre-send gate rather than a post-hoc flag, and (iv) stand up breach logging/notification and a privacy notice. Until then, treat the cloud step as a residual-PHI cross-border transfer that is not yet papered.

## 3. Key Legal Obligations by Area

### A. PHIPA (Personal Health Information Protection Act, 2004, S.O. 2004, c. 3, Sch. A)

- **The pharmacy is a health information custodian (HIC).** A "person who operates" a pharmacy (within the meaning of the *Drug and Pharmacies Regulation Act*) is a custodian under PHIPA s. 3(1) para. 4; individual pharmacists are also custodians as "health care practitioners" under para. 1. The full Act applies. https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/04p03#BK4
- **"De-identify" is a risk-based, contextual standard** (s. 2): remove information that identifies the individual *or* for which "it is reasonably foreseeable in the circumstances that it could be utilized, either alone or with other information, to identify the individual." PHIPA stops applying only when this bar is met. https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/04p03
- **"Identifying / personal health information"** (s. 4) tracks the same foreseeability test and expressly includes information identifying the provider and the drug/device supplied. https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/04p03#BK5
- **Agents (s. 17)** and **electronic service providers (s. 10(4); O. Reg. 329/04 s. 6)** — if residual PHI reaches Anthropic, Anthropic is an agent or (more aptly) a non-agent ESP. The custodian **remains fully responsible** and must bind the provider (use only as necessary, no disclosure, bind staff). https://www.canlii.org/en/on/laws/regu/o-reg-329-04/latest/o-reg-329-04.html
- **Safeguards (s. 12(1)) and information practices (s. 10):** reasonable administrative, technical, physical safeguards, expressly including electronic handling. https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/04p03#BK12
- **Breach duties (s. 12(2)–(3); O. Reg. 329/04 s. 6.3):** notify the affected individual at the first reasonable opportunity; notify the IPC in prescribed circumstances (including a "significant" breach or a "pattern"). Custodians must also **record ALL breaches** and report annual statistics to the IPC by March 1. https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/04p03#BK12
- **Written public statement of information practices (s. 16(1)).** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/04p03#BK19
- **Circle of care / assumed implied consent (s. 20(2)):** supports *using* prescription PHI to pre-fill the dispensing system — but does **not** authorize disclosing residual PHI to an arm's-length US cloud processor. https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/04p03#BK22
- **Note:** s. 10.1 (statutory electronic audit-log duty, added by Bill 188) is enacted but **awaiting regulations / not yet in force** — a pending obligation, not a current breach, but it signals the direction of travel.

### B. Cross-Border / PIPEDA

- **Transfer for processing is a "use," not a "disclosure"** — no separate patient consent required, *provided* data is used only for the collected purpose (OPC Guidelines; PIPEDA Sch. 1, Principle 4.1.3). https://www.priv.gc.ca/en/privacy-topics/airports-and-borders/gl_dab_090127/
- **Accountability (Principle 4.1.3):** the pharmacy stays responsible for PHI sent to a processor and must use contractual means to ensure a **comparable level of protection**. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/p-8.6/page-7.html
- **Safeguards proportionate to sensitivity (Principle 4.7):** health data warrants the highest level.
- **Transparency / openness (Principle 4.8):** individuals must be told their data may be processed in the US and be reachable by US courts/law-enforcement/national-security authorities. A contract cannot override foreign law.
- **US lawful access:** the CLOUD Act (18 U.S.C. § 2713) and FISA s. 702 reach data held by a US provider regardless of storage location.
- **Important overlay:** PHIPA is "substantially similar" to PIPEDA and is the **operative statute** for PHI handled by an Ontario custodian. The PIPEDA "use vs. disclosure" doctrine does **not** map cleanly onto PHIPA, which routes cross-border outsourcing through the s. 17 agent / ESP regime. Do not rely on the clean PIPEDA path alone.

### C. OCP / Ontario Pharmacy Practice

- **Scan-and-retain the ORIGINAL prescription** using software that prevents the resulting document from being edited or extracted (O. Reg. 264/16 ss. 20–21). ScriptScan's masked image is a deliberately altered version and **cannot** substitute for the unaltered original. https://ocpinfo.com/pharmacy-professionals/practice-topics/fact-sheets/record-keeping-and-scanning-requirements/
- **10-year retention** of patient-care records (O. Reg. 264/16 s. 21). https://ocpinfo.com/pharmacy-professionals/rules-and-standards-of-the-profession/practice-policies-guidelines/record-retention-disclosure-and-disposal/
- **Mandatory dispensing-record content** (DPRA s. 156(1)) — fixes the very fields ScriptScan pre-fills as content the dispenser is accountable for. https://www.canlii.org/en/on/laws/stat/rso-1990-c-h4/latest/rso-1990-c-h4.html
- **Non-delegable therapeutic check + technical check before release** (NAPRA Model Standards). Pre-filling is operationally akin to permitted data entry and does **not** encroach on professional judgment — *provided* verification is performed against the original. https://ocpinfo.com/practice_topic/scope-of-practice-pharmacy-technicians/
- **No OCP-specific AI standard exists** — a regulatory gap, not a prohibition. The workflow must be defensible under existing NAPRA PPMS, record-keeping, and PHIPA standards.
- **Custodian stays responsible for contracted-out processing**; a written agreement specifying roles is expected.

### D. IPC Ontario Guidance

- **De-Identification Guidelines for Structured Data (updated/expanded Oct 15, 2025):** removing direct identifiers is necessary but **not sufficient**; quasi-identifiers must be addressed and residual re-identification risk driven to a quantified "very low" level (targets ~5% high-impact to ~9% low-impact), with documented process, ongoing governance, and a re-identification incident procedure. https://www.ipc.on.ca/en/media/5946/download
- **Breach reporting (Health Sector Guidelines):** seven IPC-notification categories; record all breaches; annual statistics by March 1. https://www.ipc.on.ca/sites/default/files/legacy/2019/09/2019-health-privacy-breach-notification-guidelines.pdf
- **AI Scribes: Key Considerations for the Health Sector (Jan 2026):** data minimization across the AI lifecycle; vendor due diligence; contractual safeguards (use limits, no-training, retention/destruction, sub-processor controls, breach notification); **trained humans-in-the-loop** (necessary but **not sufficient**); patient transparency; PIA + threat-risk assessment. https://www.ipc.on.ca/en/resources/ai-scribes-key-considerations-health-sector
- **Third-party providers (case of note):** custodian must conduct due diligence, have a comprehensive written service agreement, and monitor compliance. https://www.ipc.on.ca/en/cases-of-note/custodians-must-ensure-phi-protected-even-when-using-third-party-providers

### E. AI-Vendor (Anthropic) Terms

- **No training on inputs/outputs** by default; standard commercial **~30-day deletion** (not zero retention). DPA with SCCs is auto-incorporated (Anthropic as processor). https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage
- **ZDR is opt-in, per-organization, sales-gated;** a **HIPAA BAA** is separate and **not** auto-incorporated. Some "Covered Models" force 30-day retention even under ZDR; policy-violation-flagged data may be retained up to **2 years** even with ZDR/BAA. https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/8956058
- **Data residency:** first-party API inference is US/global only, storage US only — **no Canadian region**. https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/data-residency
- **The local Claude Code CLI path is NOT HIPAA-eligible** and cannot be brought under a BAA; for residual-PHI workloads, use the HIPAA/ZDR-enabled Messages API exclusively.

## 4. Compliance Assessment Table

| Aspect | Status | Notes (incl. adversarial downgrades) |
|---|---|---|
| PHIPA applies (pharmacy is a custodian) | **Compliant (settled)** | Not a risk — but means no design choice can treat PHIPA as optional. Adversarial check reframed "compliant" → "PHIPA indisputably applies"; the hard questions flow *from* this. |
| Pharmacist non-delegable verification / human-in-the-loop | **Likely compliant (defensible)** | Design's strongest point. **Downgraded from "compliant"** by adversarial check: only holds if verification is independent and performed **against the original**, documented, and not a backstop for the upstream masking/disclosure risk. |
| Masked image truly "de-identified" under s. 2 | **Risk → needs lawyer** | Load-bearing weakest link. Quasi-identifiers (named prescriber + drug/SIG/date) remain; heuristic OCR can miss tokens. Clearing the IPC "very low" bar is a fact/law-intensive determination reserved for expert assessment. |
| Reliability of local OCR masking | **Gap** | Admittedly heuristic; messy/handwritten faxes have meaningful miss rates. `phi_detected` fires **after** transmission — detection, not prevention. |
| Characterization of Anthropic (agent vs ESP) | **Unclear → needs lawyer** | Most naturally an ESP (s. 10(4)/O. Reg. 329/04 s. 6); could be an agent (s. 17). Either way, paperwork/safeguard obligations are currently unmet. |
| PHIPA-compliant vendor agreement (DPA/BAA/ZDR) | **Gap → needs lawyer** | Standard commercial terms are **not** a PHIPA agent/ESP agreement. "Processor under DPA" is GDPR vocabulary, not the PHIPA instrument. BAA is separate and not auto-incorporated. |
| Data retention / "not persisted" claim | **Risk** | True only if ZDR/BAA signed **and** a ZDR-eligible model used. Default ~30-day retention; Covered Models force 30 days; flagged data up to 2 years. **"PHI not persisted" is not supportable as stated** until configuration is evidenced. |
| Use of local Claude Code CLI path | **Gap** | Claude Code is **not** HIPAA-eligible / cannot be under a BAA. Avoid for any image that may carry residual PHI. |
| Cross-border disclosure to US Anthropic | **Gap → needs lawyer** | Permissible under PHIPA *with* the right contract + safeguards + notice; currently unpapered. CLOUD Act/FISA-702 exposure must be disclosed. |
| Consent / circle-of-care basis for the data-entry use | **Likely compliant → needs lawyer** | Use is supported by s. 20(2); but circle of care does **not** authorize the US-cloud disclosure. **Downgraded:** contingent on a valid agent/ESP relationship and adequate de-identification — both unproven. Note s. 20(2) lock-box limit. |
| Safeguards (s. 12) / information practices (s. 10) | **Likely compliant → needs lawyer** | Strong in intent (in-memory, on-device, no default persistence). **Downgraded:** de-identification sufficiency and cross-border disclosure are contestable; audit-trail absence weakens posture. |
| Breach detection / logging / audit | **Gap** | No transmission log, no record of `phi_detected` events, no breach-tracking for mandatory annual statistics. |
| Breach notification readiness (s. 12(2)/(3)) | **Gap** | No detection-to-notification workflow. A `phi_detected=true` arguably means the custodian "ought to have known" of a disclosure — engaging reporting triggers. |
| Record integrity — scan/retain ORIGINAL Rx (ss. 20–21) | **Gap (workflow/integration)** | Masked image cannot be the record-of-original. Must independently capture/retain the full unaltered original in integrity-locked storage; document the separation in an SOP. |
| 10-year retention | **Likely compliant → needs lawyer** | PMS, not ScriptScan, is the system of record. **Downgraded:** benchmark store of clinical field values may be a record fragment outside the PMS; substitution risk if a masked image were ever retained. |
| Benchmark store of de-identified field values | **Likely compliant** | Low risk if genuinely non-identifying, local, access-controlled, retention-managed. Confirm rare-drug + small-catchment combos can't re-identify; disable if no operational need. |
| Encryption in transit | **Unclear** | Anthropic API is HTTPS/TLS by default (would satisfy), but not stated — confirm and document. |
| Privacy Impact Assessment / governance | **Gap** | No PIA / threat-risk assessment described; expected for AI touching PHI. Can be lightweight for an independent pharmacy. |
| Patient transparency (s. 16 / Principle 4.8) | **Gap** | No notice covering AI/US processing and lawful-access reach. |
| Re-identification prohibition (PHIPA) | **Likely compliant** | No intent to re-identify; doesn't cure the upstream residual-PHI transfer. |

## 5. Required Safeguards Before Go-Live (Prioritized)

**Tier 1 — Blockers (do not deploy without these):**

1. **Make the mask a hard, fail-closed pre-send gate.** Add an on-device coverage/confidence check that **blocks transmission or routes to manual entry** when masking confidence is low or expected identifier regions aren't found. The `phi_detected` model flag fires *after* the image has left the building and cannot be the primary control. Where possible, positionally crop known fax templates and send only the clinical region.

2. **Put a PHIPA-compliant data-processing arrangement in place with Anthropic, and configure correctly.** Sign a **BAA and enable ZDR**; route all traffic through the HIPAA-enabled org on the **Messages API**; **stop using the Claude Code CLI** path for prescription images. Pin a **ZDR-eligible model** (avoid Covered Models forcing 30-day retention). Get in writing: no-training, documented retention/TTL, named sub-processor list with notice-of-change and flow-down, breach notification, audit rights, deletion-on-termination, and data-residency where available. Document and accept the residual up-to-2-year flagged-data retention.

3. **Treat the masked image as PHI until a formal re-identification risk assessment proves otherwise.** Commission an assessment per the IPC 2025 methodology, targeting "very low" risk, explicitly covering quasi-identifiers (prescriber, drug+SIG+date, letterhead, fax header). Mask the prescriber/letterhead/header too where not clinically required; if the prescriber field is genuinely needed, proceed under the ESP/agent path rather than the de-identification exemption.

4. **Preserve the original-record duty.** Continue to scan and retain the **full, unaltered original prescription** in integrity-locked (non-editable/non-extractable) PMS storage for ≥10 years. Masking must operate only on a derived copy; document the separation in an SOP/attestation.

**Tier 2 — Required, can run in parallel:**

5. **Stand up breach logging + a breach-response workflow.** Log every transmission (timestamp, masking confidence, `phi_detected` result, PHI-free); record ALL breaches for mandatory annual IPC statistics; write a procedure mapped to s. 12(2)/(3) and O. Reg. 329/04 s. 6.3 defining who decides, how fast, and the "significant"/"pattern" triggers. Treat each `phi_detected=true` as a presumptive breach event.

6. **Document the verification step in the record.** Capture that ScriptScan pre-filled the fields and that a **named pharmacist verified each field against the original** before commit/release.

7. **Update the pharmacy's written information-practices statement (s. 16) and add patient-facing transparency** disclosing on-device de-identification, that de-identified clinical content may be processed by a **US-based AI service**, and that **US authorities could compel access** (CLOUD Act / FISA-702).

8. **Conduct and retain a lightweight PIA + threat-risk assessment** documenting the data flow, masking control, residual cross-border risk, and human-verification control — the first artifact a regulator will ask for.

**Tier 3 — Hardening / due-diligence:**

9. Confirm and document TLS in transit. Lock down the benchmark store (local, access-controlled, retention-managed; confirm no re-identifying combinations; disable if unneeded). Maintain a written accountability record (privacy officer, contracts, risk assessment, notice). Evaluate a Canadian-hosted/on-device inference alternative for the highest-sensitivity path. Engage OCP and consider a proactive IPC consultation given the novel AI-on-PHI architecture. Monitor OCP for emerging AI guidance.

## 6. Open Questions for the Lawyer

1. **De-identification adequacy:** Does the masked single-Rx image (with residual prescriber + drug + SIG + date quasi-identifiers, and admitted OCR miss-rate) meet PHIPA's "reasonably foreseeable" / IPC "very low" standard — or must every transmission be treated as a PHI disclosure?
2. **Vendor characterization:** Is Anthropic an **agent (s. 17)** or a **non-agent ESP (s. 10(4)/O. Reg. 329/04 s. 6)** here, and what specific contractual terms does each path require?
3. **Cross-border disclosure under PHIPA (not just PIPEDA):** Does sending residual PHI to a US provider require consent/notice beyond the information-practices statement, given PHIPA's stricter agent/ESP framing and out-of-Ontario considerations?
4. **Breach-trigger mechanics:** Does an emitted `phi_detected=true` flag itself satisfy the "knew or ought to have known" threshold engaging s. 12(2) individual notice and O. Reg. 329/04 s. 6.3 IPC notice? At what cumulative frequency does it become a reportable "pattern" or "significant" breach?
5. **Record-keeping interaction:** Confirm the benchmark store of de-identified clinical field values is not a patient-care record fragment that must itself be retained 10 years (or, conversely, securely destroyed), and that masking never touches the record-of-original.
6. **Circle-of-care boundary:** Confirm the lock-box (express withdrawal) handling and that no part of the workflow over-reads implied consent to cover the cloud disclosure.
7. **Adequacy of Anthropic's actual contract** (real BAA/ZDR/DPA terms, sub-processors, the 2-year flagged-data retention, Covered-Model retention) against PHIPA s. 17 / IPC service-agreement expectations.
8. **OCP posture:** Is independent pharmacist verification-against-source sufficient documentation in the absence of an OCP AI standard, and should OCP be consulted proactively?
